# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-6 (Extended v73)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); 1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse); 1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel); October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port); **November 17, 1823 (newspaper FALSE ACCOUNT: Jean Valjean drowned; body not found)**; **December 24-25, 1823 (Christmas Eve-Christmas Day, Montfermeil tavern; man in yellow coat rescued Cosette, paid Thénardier 1,500 francs, departed with child)**; **December 25-26, 1823 onward (Valjean traveled with Cosette to Dunstead harbor town in England; purchased mourning clothes for Cosette; returned to Paris at nightfall December 26 via Barrier Monceaux; took cabriolet to esplanade of Observatoire; walked through darkness toward Boulevard de l'Hôpital)**; **1824 Spring onward (lodging at decrepit building; winter passed; spring advanced; now entering summer of second year of residence)**; **CURRENT TIME: Summer of second year (approximately 1825 or 1826)—present narrative action taking place**.

## Primary Locations
M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; small village in 1823 with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier; toy-shop opposite Thénardier hostelry; Boulanger Lane; turf alley covering arch of ancient aqueduct; large clearing on right of Avenue de Bellevue); Dunstead/Kelford/Ravenmere/Staveford (English harbor towns; children chasing hoop down lane; cart with turnips at well; wind from water smelling of salt and tar; bell for vespers; parsonage with lavender; lavender bees; forge with chalked crooked sun); Ostcombe; Yarlby; Torton; Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; Toulon port; Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; Bondy; England. **Paris (1823-1826)**: Boulevard de l'Hôpital, faubourg Saint-Marceau, Salpêtrière, Porte Saint-Martin, Plat d'Etain coach office, Barrier Monceaux, esplanade of Observatoire, deserted streets adjoining Ourcine and Glacière, Marché-aux-Chevaux, Rue du Petit-Banquier, Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, Saint-Médard church. **Mouffetard quarter** (already asleep as though discipline of Middle Ages and curfew yoke still existed); Rue Censier; Rue Copeau; Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor; Rue du Puits l'Ermite; Rue de Pontoise; commissary of police office No. 14; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont church; Rue des Postes; Jardin des Plantes; Rue Poliveau. **Decrepit building (Rue des Vignes-Saint-Marcel, corner near factory between two garden walls, numbered 50 outside/52 inside)**: Mean building appearing as small thatched hovel but large as cathedral; side and gable to road; door of worm-eaten planks opening on steep muddy chalky steps; triangular hole in scantling serving as wicket and air-hole; large window with Venetian blinds, boards nailed perpendicularly; vast internal edifice resembling shed with long corridor like intestinal tube with compartments of varied dimensions; chambers received light from vague waste grounds. Ground floor serves as wagon-house for market-gardeners; no communication between ground floor and first story; flooring has neither traps nor stairs, forming building diaphragm. First story contains numerous chambers and several attics; only one occupied by old woman serving as portress and lodging manager; rest uninhabited. **Adjacent locations**: Rue de la Barrière des Gobelins; Rue Croulebarbe; Barrière Saint-Jacques; Fontainebleau barrier; road to Bicêtre; Rue de l'Ourcine; moats Saint-Victor; Jardin des Plantes; suburb of Saint-Marceau. **Great elm three-quarters dead** opposite decrepit building among trees of boulevard, almost directly facing Rue de la Barrière des Gobelins. **Odor of copperas** issued in puffs from neighboring factory roofs. **Night atmosphere**: By day ugly, evening melancholy, night sinister; darkness deep and starless or moon and wind making openings in clouds; boulevard suddenly becomes frightful; black lines sink inwards, lost in shades; solitude terrible; presentiment of meeting traps. **Summer evening/night atmosphere**: Full moon; great masses of light and shadow in streets; dark and light sides of streets; deserted lanes; Rue Poliveau region; Saint-Étienne-du-Mont striking eleven o'clock; commissary's lantern betraying followers. **LE PETIT-PICPUS DISTRICT (Chapter 6, summer year 2, current night)**: Between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; transformed by recent improvements; market-gardens, timber-yards, old buildings effaced; new wide streets, arenas, circuses, hippodraces, railway stations, prison Mazas; old names survive: Porte Saint-Jacques, Porte Paris, Barrière des Sergents, Porcherons, la Galiote, les Célestins, les Capucins, le Mail, la Bourbe, l'Arbre de Cracovie, la Petite-Pologne; monkish aspect of Spanish town; roads unpaved, streets unbuilt; wall and solitude; no shops, few vehicles, candles lighted in windows extinguished after ten o'clock; gardens, convents, timber-yards, marshes, lowly dwellings, great walls high as houses. **CUL-DE-SAC GENROT**: One exit monitored by Javert's sentinels. **RUE PETIT-PICPUS**: Protected by Javert's sentinel; illuminated by full moon. **DROIT-MUR LANE**: Nearly entirely bordered on right by mean aspect houses; on left by solitary severe building composed numerous parts growing gradually higher; very lofty on Rue Petit-Picpus side, tolerably low on Rue Polonceau side; at angle descended to mere wall forming deeply retreating niche concealed by two corners from observers. **Wall along Rue Polonceau and Rue Droit-Mur**: Extended from angle of niche to house numbered 49 on Rue Polonceau; along Rue Droit-Mur shorter fragment to gloomy building whose gable intersects, forming another retreating angle. **Gloomy building**: Somber aspect; only one window visible (two shutters covered sheet zinc, kept constantly closed); front has ancient cistern pipes of lead; various branches sketched tree-like pattern on front; ramifications imitated old leafless vine-stocks. **Niche filled by colossal wretched door**: Vast formless assemblage perpendicular planks, upper broader than lower, bound by long transverse iron strips; one side carriage gate ordinary dimensions, evidently cut not more than fifty years previously.

## Jean Valjean's Current Crisis and Flight (Summer Year 2, Continuing)
**STATUS**: ACTIVELY FLEEING with Cosette in arms. **ESCAPE ROUTE (continuing from previous night)**: Traversed Mouffetard quarter labyrinths combining Rue Censier and Rue Copeau, Rue du Battoir-Saint-Victor and Rue du Puits l'Ermite; at eleven o'clock from Saint-Étienne-du-Mont traversed Rue de Pontoise in front of commissary police office No. 14; recognized Javert perfectly leading four-man pursuit party; slipped from concealment under gate, went down Rue des Postes toward Jardin des Plantes region with Cosette; traveled through night with full moon. **CURRENT LOCATION (Chapter 6, night continuing)**: Arrived at le Petit-Picpus district between Faubourg Saint-Antoine and la Râpée; perceived timber-yards on right; crossed unsheltered illuminated space, believed himself out of danger (hunted but not followed). **PERIL RENEWED**: Turned round and perceived movement in distant darkness; recognized Javert and squad without doubt; Javert probably at commencement of street at whose end Valjean stood; Javert acquainted with labyrinth, took precautions sending man to guard exit. **ESCAPE ROUTES BLOCKED**: Examined Cul-de-Sac Genrot (cut off); examined Rue Petit-Picpus (sentinel standing, black form against white pavement illuminated by moon); to advance meant falling into sentinel's hands; to retreat meant flinging himself into Javert's arms; felt caught as in slowly contracting net; gazed heavenward in despair. **DISCOVERY OF REFUGE**: In imminent peril, sombre gloomy building (Droit-Mur lane location, ancient cistern pipes on front forming tree-like pattern) had solitary uninhabited look tempting him; conceived idea, then hope of getting inside to save himself.

## Cosette's State (Summer Year 2)
**Age**: Approximately 8.5-9 years old. **Current condition**: Carried in Valjean's arms during flight; beginning to be tired; trust in Valjean absolute; safe with him; no awareness of peril surrounding them.

## Javert's Current Status
**ACTIVELY PURSUING**: Formidable officer; confirmed as leading coordinated pursuit across le Petit-Picpus district; has squad of at least four men plus additional sentinels; acquainted with labyrinth of district streets; strategically positioned sentinels at Cul-de-Sac Genrot and Rue Petit-Picpus; commands full moon-lit night search; location: approaching from commencement of street toward which Valjean fled; actively closing net around Valjean's position.

## English Community (Harbor Towns: Kelford, Ravenmere, Staveford, Ostcombe, Yarlby, Torton, Dunstead, Wilholt)
**Kelford residents**: Volia Brackick (hummed tune from childhood while scrubbing step; fell asleep in chair before fire caught; walked long way round to avoid muddy square); Lurald Stenworth (mended torn sleeve by window, said little; married Yewyn Corrford at Ravenmere before spring was out, 1824; laughed at story nobody else found funny); Nelan (complained of aching back as usual; bought ribbon and regretted it; gave youngest daughter of Volia Brackick solemn promise to plant orchard on slope above Wilholt; laughed at story nobody else found funny). **NEW FAMILY**: A son born to Luwyn Brackick and Lurald Stenworth, called Volan Stenworth, living in Kelford; Volan laughed at story nobody else found funny; Volan Stenworth remarked "price of salt is scandal" (agreed by Volia). **Other figures**: Kadrek (read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half saints). **Physical details**: Bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; rain threatened since morning but held off; light went early; frost silvered hedges overnight; children chased hoop down lane, shrieking; cart loaded with turnips creaked past well.
